title: ASSERTION 3: God known in this life by grace-strengthened intuition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): THIRD ASSERTION. God not through an image by which His essence would be represented, but by intuition plus ye swiftest discourse belonging toward a mind by ye light belonging toward grace strengthened, in this life can be known. For this reason Paul says: we speak ye wisdom belonging toward God which none belonging toward ye rulers belonging toward this age knew, but unto us God revealed. For God thoroughly unknown things through sensible words can reveal, plus notions in our spirit form.
pass_b_english: THIRD ASSERTION. God can be known in this life not through an image by which His essence would be represented, but by intuition and the swiftest discourse of a mind strengthened by the light of grace.

For this reason Paul says: we speak God's wisdom, which none of the rulers of this age knew, but God has revealed it to us (1 Corinthians 2:7-10). For God can reveal things thoroughly unknown through sensible words, and form notions in our spirit.
source_text: ASSERTIO TERTIA. Deus, non per simulacrum quo essentia ipsius repraesentetur, sed intuitu celerimoque discursu mentis lumine gratiae corroboratae in hac vita cognosci potest. Hacpropter Paulus: Loquimur sapientiam Dei, quam nemo principum seculi cognovit, nobis autem revelavit Deus, 1 Cor. 2.7-10. Deus enim penitus ignota potest revelare per voces sensibiles, & notiones in nostro spiritu formare.
